newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks mixed in morning, red chips rebound.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks mixed in morning, red chips rebound.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were mixed in quiet early Friday trading, supported by light rotational buying in blue chips following the Dow industrials' closing record on Thursday, brokers said.
But the market focus was on China funded red-chips, which rebounded after a consolidation, they added.
The Hang Seng Index was down 1.19 points at 15,708.04. Turnover was HK$3.62 billion in the first 35 minutes.
"Properties rise and banks are firmer but utilities are slightly easier on rotational buying," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporation Index for red-chips jumped 43 points, or 1.29 percent, to 3,435.
"The red chips took a U-turn on Thursday and are higher today," Ng said.
Shanghai Industrial added HK$2.50 to HK$52.75 and China Merchants rose HK$0.60 to HK$21.25.
Trading was generally featureless on lack of fresh incentives with light buying on second and third line stocks, said Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities.
CCT Telecom led gainers added HK$0.11 to HK$1.14 and Righteous rose HK$0.04 to HK$0.47.
Brokers said trading was expected to drift sideway for the rest of the day on concerns about the Hong Kong dollar, which has come under pressure amid the Asian currency woes.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index of H-shares eased two points to 1,150 after opening slightly higher.
Shanghai Haixing eased HK$0.05 to HK$5.40. but Zhenhai Refinery was up HK$0.125 to HK$3.725.
July Hang Seng Index futures eased six points to 15,699.
